title: Governance-orchestrator unblock-roster semantics
objective: Correct invalid_unblock_roster GENERALLY so it stops over-triggering on orchestrator-produced governance tasks, without hard-coding any task id and without a bypass flag. Every existing default is preserved (missing producer invalid; non-governance orchestrator producer invalid; empty roster invalid; orchestrator-only roster invalid; producer-only roster invalid; malformed data fails closed; blocked->canceled permitted; independent-gate enforcement unchanged). Exactly ONE narrow valid case is added: a blocked task may leave blocked with producer_agent=orchestrator only when ALL of (1) task_type is exactly 'governance', (2) at least one required gate is drawn from G1/G3/G4/G5/G6, (3) reviewer_agents holds at least one usable independent reviewer (non-empty, not orchestrator, not the producer), and (4) the task stays subject to every existing directive-regime, evidence, gate, submit, verification and acceptance control. gate(), submit(), accept(), directive verification, evidence identity, and producer-versus-reviewer separation must not weaken.
business_reason: Owner directive D-004 amendment 9 (source-010, rows D-004-R332/R344-R361): the owner REJECTED naming a false producer for M0-T027 (option a) and REJECTED abandoning it (option c), and AUTHORIZED a narrow independently-reviewed control-plane correction (option b). M0-T027's honest producer IS the main-session orchestrator (ADR-005 reserves teammate dispatch, pilot execution and integration to the main session), its evidence is complete and merged, and it already carries three usable independent reviewers - so the guard's stated rationale (an independent gate would otherwise be unsatisfiable) does not hold for it. The purpose is to recognize the orchestrator as the truthful producer of orchestrator-produced governance evidence when independent review remains structurally possible.

acceptance_scenarios: AS-1 (executable, D-004-R362): an ordinary NON-governance task (e.g. task_type='engineering') with producer_agent='orchestrator' is still REFUSED at the blocked->in_progress transition; the pre-existing regression test for this remains green and unmodified in substance.

AS-2 (executable, D-004-R363): a task with task_type='governance', producer_agent='orchestrator', at least one required gate from G1/G3/G4/G5/G6, and at least one usable independent reviewer CAN leave blocked; invalid_unblock_roster returns None and progress() performs the transition.

AS-4 (executable, D-004-R365): task_type='governance' + producer_agent='orchestrator' + reviewer_agents==['orchestrator'] is REFUSED.

risks: Over-broad fix: a helper rewritten to key on 'producer is orchestrator' alone would silently permit non-governance orchestrator producers. AS-1 and AS-5 are the guards; the four conditions must be conjunctive.

Fail-open on malformed data: treating a non-list reviewer_agents or required_gates as 'empty' could flip a refusal into a pass. AS-6 requires an explanatory refusal, not a traceback and not a silent allow.
Scope escape: docs/GATES_AND_CHECKPOINTS.md is conditional. Touching it without a real contradicted invariant is an unauthorized change under D-004-R342/R343.

Producer independence: backend-engineer must not review its own change; all four reviewers (code-reviewer, security-reviewer, control-plane-verifier, directive-compliance-verifier) are distinct from the producer and from each other.

Collateral weakening: the required independent-gate check (condition 2) reads required_gates, which gate() also consumes. Any refactor there risks changing gate enforcement - AS-9/AS-12 exist to catch it.
allowed_paths_note: D-004-R342 fixes this task's scope to exactly these paths. docs/GATES_AND_CHECKPOINTS.md is CONDITIONAL: it may be touched ONLY if the corrected semantics actually contradict a stated invariant there; if it does not, the file must remain byte-identical and the producer report must state that explicitly. project-control/tasks/M0-T033.json is an ORCHESTRATOR LIFECYCLE path written only by tools/project_control.py (claim/progress/submit/gate/accept); it is never a producer write target and is listed so a containment diff has no unexplained escape. It is authorized by D-004-R342 ("M0-T033 own packet AND REPORTS") and is an ORCHESTRATOR LIFECYCLE artifact, never a producer write target; it is added here so a containment diff has no unexplained escape. project-control/state.json is likewise written automatically by sync_state() during the orchestrator lifecycle - its forbidden_paths entry is retained and qualified below, binding the PRODUCER only. This was an orchestrator packet-drafting defect, NOT a producer escape: the producer commit 6592b89 touched exactly three files, all inside allowed_paths, verified by three independent reviewers.
